meta._doc: Hero output (hero.json). ONE crafted cover per run — the animated

hero.id: des_hero_video   // FIXED. The single provenance id of the cover's one Verify hit. Always des_hero_video — reuse the Designer prefix, never a new one.
hero.kind: video | image   // video on every animated rung (0-4); image ONLY on the recorded rung-5 static fallback.
hero.backs: teaser   // the section the hero backs — always the opening 'teaser' beat. Lets the Cinematographer stage it as cin_00 (backs:'teaser').
hero.subject_is_real_public_figure: boolean   // true => the source still depicts a recognizable real public figure, so image2video was routed to Kling (Veo/Wan refuse, code 15236754).

source.origin: interactive_passthrough | scout_still | scout_real_figure | scout_stock_clip | abstract_still | static_fallback   // which ladder rung resolved (matches meta.source_ladder_rung's name).
source.still_ref: sct_03 | des_07 | null   // the registered Scout sct_xx / Designer des_xx the motion was built from (the i2v input still, or the stock clip's own registered item). null when a text2image abstract still was generated fresh and is itself this hero item.
source.model: google/veo-3.1-fast | kwaivgi/kling-v3.0-std | openai/gpt-5.4-image-2 | null   // the generation model used (i2v model on rungs 1-4; text2image model on rung 4's still; null on a pure ffmpeg/passthrough/stock path).
source.tool: image2video | text2image | ffmpeg_kenburns | none   // the actual render path. ffmpeg_kenburns = the non-AI camera-move fallback (real-face hero when even Kling is unavailable).
source.prompt: motion-only prompt for image2video ('flags ripple, smoke drifts; subject and faces held still, no camera shake'), or the text2image still prompt; '' for a stock clip / passthrough.
source.duration: 4 | 6 | 8   // the OpenRouter video duration (ONLY 4/6/8 are accepted). Omit/null for a static fallback or a stock clip of fixed length.
source.fallback_used: kenburns | static_poster | null   // copied from the image2video script's printed FALLBACK_USED=<rung>; null when the chosen model rendered cleanly. static_poster => the render degraded to a still and kind became 'image'.

assets.video_webm: assets/teaser.webm   // VP9 web copy (the optimize_assets.py _web output). null on the static rung-5 fallback.
assets.video_mp4: assets/teaser_web.mp4   // H.264 fallback for the <video>. null on the static rung-5 fallback.
assets.poster: assets/teaser.jpg // the frame-0 / source still — ALWAYS present (it is the

hero.reduced_motion_fallback: assets/teaser.jpg   // the still shown under prefers-reduced-motion and JS-off — normally the same file as assets.poster. ALWAYS set (a moving hero must degrade to a readable still).

furniture.headline_band: the headline/kicker band rendered over the cover (text the Programmer paints in the .teaser overlay), e.g. 'Who wins 2026?'
furniture.kicker: the small eyebrow above the headline, or null.
furniture.credit_line: the visible source/AI-likeness credit shown small on the cover (pulled from the still_ref's license/identity, or the AI-likeness disclosure for a generated still).
decorative: an ARRAY of purely-decorative furniture items (VS monogram, particle canvas, FC-26-style chips, scrim) — each rendered pointer-events:none with NO data-* attribute so the Verify engine ignores them. [] when the cover has no decorative furniture.

hero.interactive_overlay_ref: int_01 | null   // set to 'int_01' ONLY on rung 0 (interactive-hero passthrough): the Interaction Engineer owns the pick-a-side overlay, the Hero renders the animated backdrop behind it. null on every other rung.

verify.hit_target: .teaser   // the SINGLE Verify hit selector — one overlay carries provenance for the whole cover.
verify.data_attr: data-des   // the provenance attribute on the hit target (reuse the Designer prefix).
verify.class_marker: teaser   // the class the .teaser overlay carries; the rest of the cover (video + furniture, wrapped in .cin-stage) is auto-excluded by isDecorative().

hero.disclosure: the honest provenance/AI-likeness line, e.g. 'Image AI-generated; motion = a camera move on the still (not AI video of a real person)' for a cinemagraph, or 'Photo: <author> / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0) — identity verified' for a fetched-still hero. Rendered in the credit_line.
hero.publish_blocker: boolean   // true ONLY when the cover uses a rights-encumbered asset (a copyrighted self-hosted stock clip → demo-only). Forces the Auditor's advisory publish-gate + the Programmer's 'demo-only — license or swap before publishing' credit. false on every license-clean / AI-generated / fetched-clean path.
hero.ip_record_ref: references/hero_recipes.json#ip_record   // pointer to the IP record (Veo/Wan refusal code 15236754, Kling works, the fallback ladder, the AI-likeness disclosure, the stock-clip publish-gate).

_field_notes.one_cover: There is exactly ONE hero per run. `hero` is a single object, not a dict of ids. Its provenance is des_hero_video (reused — never a 6th prefix).
_field_notes.kind_image_is_the_floor: kind:'video' on rungs 0-4 (the cover is animated by default). kind:'image' is reachable ONLY on rung 5, the recorded static fallback, when every animation rung degraded (fallback_used:'static_poster' OR no clip could be sourced) — and then the assets.poster is shipped as the with a recorded media_blocker.
_field_notes.single_verify_hit: The whole cover routes provenance through ONE .teaser overlay (data-des=des_hero_video). The
_field_notes.cin_stage_wrapper: The Programmer always wraps the cover in .cin-stage: cinematic-ON => it is the cin_00 layer of the live cinematic stage; cinematic-OFF => a degenerate <div class='cin-stage hero-only-stage'> that still carries the poster backdrop. Either way the cover is inside a .cin-stage, so it is verify-immune.
_field_notes.assets_budget: Run optimize_assets.py after render; the web-weight cover (webm+mp4) must be < 3 MB. A heavier upscaled hero is tolerated only when the page can afford it (see hero_recipes.json), but the default is the optimized _web copies.
_field_notes.interactive_overlay_ref: Non-null ONLY on rung 0. When the Editor placed the centerpiece interactive on the teaser (editor.json.interactives.hero.section=='teaser'), the interaction IS the Interaction Engineer's int_01; the Hero renders the moving backdrop and yields the click surface to int_01 — the two coexist (Hero owns the video + static furniture, the Interaction Engineer owns the pick-a-side overlay).
_field_notes.publish_blocker_gate: validate.py Section 8 already HARD-errors a publish_blocker asset with no swap target — a rights-encumbered hero (copyrighted stock clip) must carry the publish_note via its registered des_ asset. A license-clean / AI-generated / fetched-clean cover sets publish_blocker:false.
